evidence: Base existence AUC was 0.473/0.485/0.463 in discovery/validation/holdout; strict temporal validity was 0.467/0.497/0.451.
limitation: Direction is weakly negative and is not a useful positive screen.
v1_comparison: Does not overturn the V1 weak-scalar conclusion.

evidence: Peak-age AUC was 0.422/0.441/0.436; winners were somewhat younger when a base existed.
limitation: Only 31-40% of winner/control events had an available canonical base and the holdout cluster CI included 0.5.
v1_comparison: Canonical age adds a hypothesis but not a robust decision feature.

v1_comparison: Canonical mass does not change the prior weak-feature conclusion.

limitation: Low coverage and validation direction opposed discovery/holdout.
v1_comparison: Canonical prominence does not provide stable launch separation.

evidence: T-5/T-10 changes in peak location and band width separated validation/holdout among available bases; holdout location-change AUC reached 0.765-0.785.
limitation: Winner coverage was only 11-22%, raw levels were weak, and longer-lead levels did not strengthen consistently.
v1_comparison: Adds local confirmation information but not a broad pre-launch predictor.

evidence: Twenty-session base presence was lower before winners in validation/holdout (AUC 0.461/0.428).
limitation: Discovery was near null; binding-run age reversed direction and only 31-40% had exact values.
v1_comparison: Mixed temporal evidence does not justify replacing V1 conclusions.

evidence: Twenty-session split/merge/lost counts separated discovery and holdout; holdout AUC was about 0.61-0.62.
limitation: Validation was null or opposite, so the effect is regime-dependent.
v1_comparison: Adds a lifecycle hypothesis, not a stable standalone predictor.

evidence: Ambiguity-rate AUC was 0.544/0.545/0.569 and the holdout symbol-cluster CI was 0.527-0.611; T-20 ambiguity direction was consistent across splits.
limitation: Effect size is modest and single-day ambiguity is weaker than persistence.
v1_comparison: This is the clearest canonical V3 temporal increment over simple V1 scalars.

evidence: Profit-ratio changes and same-day levels moved strongly near selected troughs; concentration was inconsistent across splits.
limitation: Lead profiles frequently attenuated or changed direction, indicating reaction to the immediate price dislocation.
v1_comparison: Broadly retains the V1 conclusion that simple scalar state is weak before launch.

evidence: T-5 cost-anchor changes generalized strongly in validation/holdout; holdout AUC was 0.764-0.777 with full coverage.
limitation: The separation largely vanished at T-5/T-10 raw leads and is mechanically price-relative.
v1_comparison: Useful as near-launch confirmation, not evidence that a durable chip-state threshold was discovered.

evidence: Model-spread p50 had a holdout AUC near 0.59.
limitation: Split stability and effect size were insufficient for a strong classification.
